newsitem.title: USA: Mass. governor to push for corporate tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Mass. governor to push for corporate tax cuts.

text.p: Gov. William Weld of Massachusetts on Wednesday said he would push for several tax cuts for corporations this year.
"We think that corporate income taxes are due for another cut this year," Weld told the Massachusetts Taxpayers Foundation, a non-profit group that provides research on the state's economy.

Weld said the tax code penalizes Massachusetts-based insurance companies and should be changed along the lines of the single sales tax introduced for financial and industrial companies over the last couple of years.

The governor urged the repeal of the state's telecommunications sales tax and called for a job-training tax credit. Weld also proposed a cut in the tax on unearned income to 5.9 percent from 12 percent.
Weld said the proposed cuts and credits would add to 15 tax reductions passed since he was elected in 1990.
"Our economy for the last six years has been growing like corn in Kansas," he said. "We really have put R-I-P on the tombstone on the term 'Taxachusetts'," he said.
